title: Grants Posthumous Pardon to Jack Johnson
description_short: Trump granted a posthumous pardon to boxer Jack Johnson.
description_medium: President Donald Trump granted a posthumous pardon to boxer Jack Johnson on May 24, 2018. Johnson had died in 1946, decades after his conviction and imprisonment. The pardon recognized Johnson after his death but could not change the years he spent in prison. The specific conviction and the circumstances surrounding it remain unclear.
description_long: President Donald Trump granted a posthumous pardon to boxer Jack Johnson on May 24, 2018. Johnson, the first Black heavyweight champion, had died in 1946 after decades of fame, discrimination, and legal persecution. His 1913 conviction for transporting a woman across state lines was widely criticized as racially motivated. The pardon came after years of public advocacy, including support from members of Congress and boxing figures. It recognized the injustice of the conviction long after Johnson could benefit personally; he could not be released or restored to life. The pardon became a symbolic acknowledgment of a case that reflected how federal law had been used against a Black athlete during the Jim Crow era.
